newsitem.title: GERMANY: Positions of two sides in German tax talks detailed.
newsitem.headline: Positions of two sides in German tax talks detailed.

text.p: Following is a guide to where Chancellor Helmut Kohl's coalition government and opposition Social Democrats stood on Wednesday in their talks on sweeping German tax reforms intended to boost job-creating investment.
The two sides held a rare tax "summit" on Monday and a working group of six negotiators will meet again on Friday. The coalition has set an Easter deadline for finding a compromise:
Cut top rate to 39 pct (vs 53 pct) Opposes big cut
Cut bottom rate to 15 pct (vs 26) Cut to under 20 pct
Cut on retained profits to 35 pct Agrees
Cut on distributed profits to 25 Opposes, wants
Lower solidarity surcharge revenue Not subject to SPD
Wants to abolish 70 tax breaks, Agrees with most, but

NOTE - Coalition plans to cut the 7.5 percent solidarity income tax surcharge in 1998 by two points, causing a revenue fall of 7.5 billion marks. This does not require SPD support to take effect.
-- Douglas Busvine, Bonn newsroom, 49-228-26097150 ($ = 1.670 German Marks)
